problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}c \\ d\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the vector $\,x=[\begin{aligned}-4+9\text{i} \\ 1+8\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $bc-ad?$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing Components of the Real and Imaginary Parts of a Complex Vector
examples.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041865/assets/19d1bb5ad60407748a9c624dee20931c3c70a4bbc3727c4172cfb40384ab6a72.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041865/assets/f7539ad7301462681681e738b905633b7aa73ca65b5512063e32fa22bcdc0d09.png) are the real and imaginary parts of the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041865/assets/a7976c73a0aeb9f286a281c193b3a00b38e8bc0fa36a30e985fe1e8f80d7796b.png) what is the value of $ab+cd?$
examples.worked_solution:
For the given vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041865/assets/4d6fc79d41790b29a966f7a3303329ab1b778856991ad5b3b85ee3965fce2e33.png) we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =[\begin{aligned}-3+7\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(x)}+\text{i}\,{{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $a=-3, b=5, c=7$ and $d=-2,$ which implies that

$$
ab+cd=(-3) \cdot 5 + 7 \cdot (-2) = -29.
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}4+3\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i} \\ 5\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{4+3\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2-2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{5\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4-3\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} \\ -5\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
